### FINDING 1 — NONFATAL — location: step 2.2 (Verification)
CLAIM AS WRITTEN: "...hence $0 < 1/(j+1) \le 1/n < \varepsilon$... [step 1.1, L3, L4, L5, L6, L7, L8]" — `L8` ("Trichotomy of the order on ℝ") was the citation added by the repair.
WHY IT FAILS: it doesn't fail; it just isn't tightly necessary. The chain `0 < n ≤ j+1 → 0 < 1/(j+1) ≤ 1/n` is licensed by `[L4]`'s order-reversal fact together with ordinary transitivity of `≤`/`<`, not specifically by trichotomy. (In fact `j ≥ n` as naturals gives the strictly sharper `n < j+1`, making the written `≤` a valid but non-tight weakening — also harmless.)
WHAT WOULD FIX IT: nothing needs fixing; this is exactly the "minor citational quirk" the brief says to leave alone. Noted only for completeness since it's the one line the repair touched mathematically.

Steps 4.1–5.1 (the point is $0$, hence the intersection is $\{0\}$) are immediate and correct.
